problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013598/assets/2ffa9585853d1230c9664a27dffcd832aec5cdff3fa1d3f01c9012d2835d101e.png)

Find the total area of the region between the curve $y={x}^{2}-2x$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=3,$ as shown above.
worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x & =0 \\ x(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Since $2\in [0,3],$ we have two regions: 

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=2.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=2$ to $x=3.$

Notice that the region for $x\in [0,2]$ lies completely below the $x$-axis. Hence, the value of

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x)\,\text{d}x
$$

will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{2}+{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[{2}^{3}-{0}^{3}]+[{2}^{2}-{0}^{2}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[8-0]+4 \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}+4 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x\in [2,3],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{2}^{3}({x}^{2}-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{2}^{3}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{2}^{3}-{x}^{2}\,{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{3}^{3}-{2}^{3}]-[{3}^{2}-{2}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[27-8]-[9-4] \\  & =\frac{19}{3}-5 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the total area is

$$
A={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{4}{3}+\frac{4}{3}=\frac{8}{3}.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we find the intersections of the curve with the x-axis: x2−2x=0x(x−2)=0x=0,2

Since 2∈[0,3], we have two regions:

  • The area between the curve and the x-axis from x=0 to x=2.

  • The area between the curve and the x-axis from x=2 to x=3.

Notice that the region for x∈[0,2] lies completely below the x-axis. Hence, the value of ∫aby(x)dx=∫02(x2−2x)dx will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by A1=−∫02(x2−2x)dx=−∫02x2dx+2∫02xdx=−13x3|02+x2|02=−13[23−03]+[22−02]=−13[8−0]+4=−83+4=43.

For x∈[2,3], we have A2=∫23(x2−2x)dx=∫23x2dx−2∫23xdx=13x3|23−x2|23=13[33−23]−[32−22]=13[27−8]−[9−4]=193−5=43.

Finally, the total area is A=A1+A2=43+43=83.
